title: CPR – Adult
summary: For an adult who is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Call for help, push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, and use an AED as soon as one arrives.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} now and get an AED
when: Unresponsive and not breathing normally – call immediately, put the phone on speaker and start CPR
Send someone for an AED; if you are alone with a phone, do not leave the casualty – call on speaker and start CPR

steps.title: Check it is safe and check response
steps.text: Shake their shoulders and shout. If no response, shout for help.

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.text: Open the airway (head tilt, chin lift) and check for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping or occasional breaths are not normal – treat as not breathing.

steps.title: Call {EMERGENCY} and send for an AED
steps.text: Put the phone on speaker. The dispatcher can guide you.

steps.title: Start chest compressions
steps.text: Kneel beside them. Place the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest (lower half of the breastbone), the other hand on top, arms straight, shoulders over your hands.
points: Let the chest come fully back up after each compression

steps.title: Give rescue breaths if trained (30:2)
steps.text: After 30 compressions, open the airway and give 2 breaths, each over about 1 second, just enough to make the chest rise. Then go straight back to 30 compressions.
points: If you are not trained or not willing to give breaths, do continuous compressions only (hands-only CPR)
Use a pocket mask or barrier if available

steps.title: Use the AED as soon as it arrives
steps.text: Switch it on and follow the voice prompts. Attach the pads to the bare chest as shown on the pads. Make sure nobody touches the casualty during analysis and shock.
points: Restart compressions immediately after a shock or if no shock is advised

steps.title: Keep going
steps.text: Continue CPR until professional help takes over, the person starts breathing normally, or you are physically unable to continue. If there is another rescuer, swap every 2 minutes to keep compressions effective.
points: If they start breathing normally, place them in the recovery position and keep checking breathing

warningSigns: No response and no normal breathing
Gasping or very slow, irregular breaths
Seizure-like movements immediately after collapse can occur in cardiac arrest – check breathing
doNot: Do not delay compressions to look for a pulse if you are not trained to do so
Do not stop compressions for more than a few seconds
Do not lean on the chest between compressions
Do not be afraid of hurting them – broken ribs are possible but cardiac arrest is fatal without CPR

sources.title: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
